executive_summary: NVIDIA's latest reported quarter is Q2 FY27 (ended 2026-07-26, released 2026-08-26); Q3 FY27 has not yet been reported per the IR page. Revenue was $96.2bn, up 17.9% q/q and 105.9% y/y, driven by Data Center ($89.0bn, +18% q/q per the release) with the newly labelled Edge Computing segment at $7.2bn (+13% q/q, +27% y/y). GAAP gross margin held at 75.0% (74.9% in Q1, 72.4% a year ago) and the print ties out internally to within rounding; GAAP operating margin rose to 66.2% from 65.6% q/q and 60.8% y/y as opex grew 10.3% q/q against revenue growth of 17.9%. GAAP net income rose only 2.3% q/q because Q1 was inflated by large equity-securities gains, whereas non-GAAP EPS of $2.22 rose 18.7% q/q and 119.8% y/y. The weak spot is cash: operating cash flow (summary-level, PROVISIONAL) fell 52.2% q/q to $24.1bn and free cash flow fell 56.0% to $21.3bn, only 35.8% of GAAP net income, while about $26.0bn was returned to shareholders, about 21.8% more than FCF. Q3 guidance of $108.0bn +/-2% implies 12.2% q/q growth at the midpoint (decelerating from 17.9%), gross margin guided to 74.0% +/-50bp (down from 75.0%), and still no China Data Center compute assumed. Thesis read-through: demand and operating leverage remain intact; what changed is decelerating sequential growth, a modest margin step-down, a sharp cash-conversion drop that needs explaining, rising earnings exposure to mark-to-market equity holdings, and an unread CEO-transition announcement dated 2026-11-12. No consensus was available, so no beat/miss is asserted. Evidence is caller-supplied and not re-read from the original in this run, so quality is PROVISIONAL.

key_findings.finding: Growth remained very strong but is decelerating sequentially: revenue +17.9% q/q and +105.9% y/y in Q2 FY27, while the Q3 FY27 midpoint guide of $108.0bn implies +12.2% q/q (range bounds +/-2% around the midpoint). Data Center at $89.0bn (+18% q/q) is the overwhelming driver; compute/networking split not printed.

Cash conversion fell sharply: operating cash flow -52.2% q/q to $24.1bn and FCF -56.0% q/q to $21.3bn despite higher profits; FCF conversion of GAAP net income dropped to 35.8% from 83.3% in Q1 FY27 and 50.9% a year ago. Cash-flow lines are from a summary of a truncated page (PROVISIONAL), so the cause (working capital, inventory/supply prepayments or tax timing) is unexplained and the figures need confirming against the 10-Q.

Operating leverage and margins held at peak levels: GAAP gross margin 75.0% (ties out to an implied 74.98% from operating income plus opex), GAAP operating margin 66.2% vs 65.6% q/q and 60.8% y/y, with GAAP opex +10.3% q/q against revenue +17.9%. Q3 guide steps gross margin down to 74.0% +/-50bp and opex up 9.4% to about $9.2bn GAAP.

GAAP earnings quality is distorted by mark-to-market equity holdings: GAAP net income exceeded non-GAAP net income in Q2 FY27 ($59.7bn vs $54.0bn) and Q1 GAAP net income ($58.3bn) exceeded GAAP operating income ($53.5bn), consistent with net equity-securities gains of $7.8bn (Q2) and $15.9bn (Q1) per the summary. Marketable equity securities grew to $42.8bn from $12.9bn at FY-end, so GAAP EPS (+2.9% q/q) understates operating momentum while non-GAAP EPS (+18.7% q/q) tracks it.

Capital returns stepped up and now exceed free cash flow: about $26.0bn returned in Q2 FY27 (repurchases $19.7bn, +103% y/y; dividends $6.0bn vs $0.2bn a year ago, with a $0.25 quarterly dividend), about 21.8% above FCF; about $99.0bn of authorization remains. Balance-sheet liquidity remains large (cash $22.4bn, marketable debt securities $34.1bn).

One-offs and disclosure changes: an H20 charge/(release) footnote referencing $4.5bn is incompletely captured; China Data Center compute remains excluded from guidance (upside optionality, not in numbers); Edge Computing is a new segment label replacing separate Gaming/ProViz/Auto disclosure, which breaks historical segment comparability; and a CEO transition release dated 2026-11-12 exists but was not read.

scenarios.name: bull
scenarios.narrative: Q3 FY27 lands at or above the top of the +/-2% range with gross margin at the top of 74.0% +/-50bp; Q2 cash shortfall proves to be timing (supply prepayments/receivables) and reverses; China compute adds upside not in guidance.

scenarios.name: base
scenarios.narrative: Q3 FY27 delivers near the $108.0bn midpoint (+12.2% q/q) with gross margin about 74.0%; operating margin broadly stable as opex grows about 9% q/q; FCF conversion partially recovers.

scenarios.name: bear
scenarios.narrative: Sequential growth slows toward the bottom of the range, gross margin drifts to the low end (73.5%) on mix/new-product ramps, working-capital build persists so capital returns keep exceeding FCF, and equity-securities marks turn negative, hitting GAAP EPS; leadership transition adds execution uncertainty.

counterarguments: The cash-flow weakness may be an artefact of the truncated-page summary; if the 10-Q shows different CFO/FCF, finding 2 falls away.
Decelerating q/q growth from a much larger base is normal and the guide may be conservative, as with prior NVIDIA guides; without consensus the deceleration cannot be called a disappointment.
A one-point gross-margin step-down guided for Q3 may reflect new-product ramp costs that historically recovered, rather than pricing pressure.

GAAP net income benefiting from equity marks inflates Q1/Q2 GAAP figures; investors relying on GAAP P/E overstate earnings power, while non-GAAP figures may understate the economic value of the investment portfolio.

risks.risk: Cash conversion: FCF fell to 35.8% of GAAP net income while ~$26.0bn was returned; if persistent, the return pace depends on drawing down the liquidity pool.
Concentration: Data Center is $89.0bn of $96.2bn revenue; hyperscaler capex cycles directly drive results.
Earnings volatility from a $42.8bn marketable equity-securities book marked through GAAP net income.
China export restrictions: guidance assumes no China Data Center compute; H20 charge history ($4.5bn reference, wording incomplete) shows inventory/charge risk from policy changes.
Leadership: a CEO transition announcement dated 2026-11-12 was not read; its terms and timing are an unassessed thesis risk.

unknowns: Consensus estimates for Q2 FY27 and Q3 FY27 (no licensed connector): no beat/miss can be stated.
CFO commentary and earnings-call transcript (not fetched): management explanation of the cash-flow drop, gross-margin guide and segment drivers is missing.
Data Center compute vs networking split and the composition of the new Edge Computing segment.
Exact H20 charge/(release) amounts by quarter and their gross-margin effect (footnote incomplete).
Sign and classification of the equity-securities gains line (summary unclear) and the reconciliation from GAAP to non-GAAP net income.
Working-capital, inventory, supply-commitment and capex detail behind the 52.2% q/q CFO decline (10-Q not retrieved; EDGAR fetch failed).
Content of the 2026-11-12 CEO transition release.
Q3 FY27 results date and outcome (not yet reported as of 2026-11-14).

implications.text: Treat Q2 FY27 as strong on growth and operating margin but with an unexplained cash-conversion drop and a modest margin step-down guide; read the 2026-11-12 CEO transition release and the Q3 FY27 print (due shortly) before relying on this review. No consensus was available, so nothing here establishes beat/miss.

Challenge: (1) whether the CFO/FCF figures (summary-level) hold against the 10-Q; (2) the gap between GAAP and non-GAAP EPS driven by equity-securities marks; (3) whether 12.2% implied q/q growth plus a 74.0% gross-margin guide is consistent with operating-margin stability given opex growing 9.4%.

Results show continued very rapid growth and the highest margins of the three quarters reviewed, but cash generation fell sharply in the quarter and a CEO change was announced on 2026-11-12. Research only; no rating or action.

Fundamental inputs available as PROVISIONAL figures: revenue +105.9% y/y, GAAP operating margin 66.2%, non-GAAP EPS $2.22, Q3 guide $108.0bn +/-2%, FCF conversion 35.8%. Flag the leadership-transition event for the news analyst.
